question: Does translation-invariant polyphase max pooling keep a classifier's accuracy more stable under small input shifts than standard stride-2 max pooling on the digits dataset?
method: Baseline: standard stride-2 max-pooled features with standardized logistic regression (C tuned by 5-fold CV on training data). Improved: polyphase max-pooled features (elementwise max of the four stride-2 sub-grids plus the sub-grids themselves, 80 features) with a standardized RBF SVM whose C and gamma are tuned by 5-fold CV on training data. Both trained on unshifted train images; test accuracy averaged over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px).

dataset.name: Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits (scikit-learn load_digits)

metric_name: mean test accuracy over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px in each direction)
baseline: Standard 2x2 max pooling with stride 2 (8x8 -> 4x4) followed by standardized logistic regression.
improved: Dense stride-1 2x2 max pooling with polyphase sub-grids (elementwise max plus separate sub-grid features, 80 values per image) followed by a standardized RBF SVM tuned by CV on training data.
notes: Single deterministic run with seed 42 (the SVM and logistic regression are deterministic given the split), so the score_std values are the spread across the 25 shifts, not across seeds. The baseline is a stand-in for CNN pooling; the paper's exact polyphase selection rule was not re-implemented. The improved model changes both the pooled features and the classifier (RBF SVM), so any gain reflects the combination and not pooling alone; the elementwise max over the four phases also enlarges the effective pooling window to about 3x3. Hyperparameters were chosen only by 5-fold CV on the training set; the test set was used once for final scores. Only 8x8 images were used, so results may not transfer to deep CNNs.
